## Raw data quality metrics and Bad channel detection

This (optional) step computes IBL's quality metrics on raw recordings before destructive or corrective processing. 

It also uses IBL's bad channel detection algorithm to flag bad channels. These can be passed to the preprocessing for removal or interpolation. Bad channel detection is run after high-pass filtering at 300 Hz.
This is because bandpass filtering removes the high-frequencies used for noisy channel detection.

The metrics and bad channel detection results are written to the `RAW_DATA_METRICS_DIR` in the PROJECT_PATH.

**Inputs**

- a [`RAW_DATA_PATH`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path), [`RAW_DATA_PATH_LIST`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path-list), [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec), or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC_LIST`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec-list)
- a [`CONFIG`](outputs.qmd#config)
- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path)

**Outputs**

- [`RAW_DATA_QUALITY_METRICS`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-quality-metrics) saved to the [`RAW_DATA_METRICS_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#raw-data-metrics-dir)
- [`RAW_DATA_QUALITY_PLOTS`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-quality-plots) saved to the [`RAW_DATA_METRICS_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#raw-data-metrics-dir)
- [`BAD_CHANNEL_IDS`](outputs.qmd#bad-channel-ids) and [`BAD_CHANNEL_LABELS`](outputs.qmd#bad-channel-labels), saved to the [`RAW_DATA_METRICS_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#raw-data-metrics-dir).

<details>
<summary><strong>Checks</strong></summary>

- This algorithm was developed for Neuropixels probes. Different settings should be recommended for probes with lower channel counts.

</details>

## Artifact detection

This (optional) step can detect two types of artifact:
- saturation artifacts, detected before preprocessing
- other artifacts detected after high-pass filtering (e.g. envelope).

see [`detect_and_remove_artifacts()`](https://spikeinterface.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#spikeinterface.preprocessing.detect_and_remove_artifacts) for details.

These detected periods (stored in [`EVENT_PERIODS_CSV`](outputs.qmd#event-periods-csv)) are used in [Preprocessing](#preprocessing) to zero or otherwise remove the periods. 

**Inputs**

- a [`RAW_DATA_PATH`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path), [`RAW_DATA_PATH_LIST`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path-list), [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec), or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC_LIST`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec-list)
- a [`CONFIG`](outputs.qmd#config)
- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path)

**Outputs**

- an [`EVENT_PERIODS_CSV`](outputs.qmd#event-periods-csv), saved to the [`ARTIFACT_DETECTION_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#artifact-detection-dir)

## Artifact curation

This (optional) stepprovides the user with the option to curate the automatically detected artifacts. This step is not automated, and typically more hands-on and requires a dedicated walkthrough in the documentation. It will entail the user loading their data into viewephys (applying the preprocessing beforehand as desired).

**Inputs**

- a [`RAW_DATA_PATH`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path) or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec)
- an [`EVENT_PERIODS_CSV`](outputs.qmd#event-periods-csv)
- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path)

**Outputs**

- an [`EVENT_PERIODS_CURATED_CSV`](outputs.qmd#event-periods-curated-csv), saved to the [`ARTIFACT_DETECTION_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#artifact-detection-dir)

## Preprocessing

Preprocesses the recording, supporting: 

- Bad channel removal or interpolation (interpolation after filtering).
- Phase shift correction.
- TEMPORAL_FILTER steps 
- Artifact period filling with zeros, noise, or another configured strategy.
- - COMMON_REFERENCE steps
- Motion correction.
- Inter-session alignment when the input is a list of recordings.
- Whitening.

**Inputs**

- a [`RAW_DATA_PATH`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path), [`RAW_DATA_PATH_LIST`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path-list), [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec), or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC_LIST`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec-list)
- a [`CONFIG`](outputs.qmd#config)
- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path)
- (optional) [`EVENT_PERIODS_CSV`](outputs.qmd#event-periods-csv) or [`EVENT_PERIODS_CURATED_CSV`](outputs.qmd#event-periods-curated-csv), loaded from the [`ARTIFACT_DETECTION_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#artifact-detection-dir)

**Outputs**

- a [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec) or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC_LIST`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec-list) (of preprocessed recordings). This may be written to disk in the `PREPROCESSING_DIR` depending on CONFIG settings.
- a [`PREPROCESSING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#preprocessing-dir). This contains metadata and quality-metrics related to the preprocessing. 

<details>
<summary><strong>Preprocessing checks</strong></summary>

- Apply phase-shift correction when the probe supports it.
- For multi-session processing, use the same set of channels across sessions.
- Do not re-run whitening or motion correction in the sorter if already run through SpikeInterface preprocessing.
- Warn when high-density-specific methods, such as motion correction or bad channel detection, are used on 32- or 64-channel recordings.

</details>

## Spike sorting

The spike sorting step, made very simple thanks to SpikeInterface:

**Inputs**

- a [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec) or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC_LIST`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec-list),
  OR a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path) containing a [`PREPROCESSING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#preprocessing-dir) with saved recording.
- a [`CONFIG`](outputs.qmd#config)
- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path) containing a [`PREPROCESSING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#preprocessing-dir). This is used to store outputs and cross-check the metadata of the passed recording to the on-disk project.

**Outputs**

- a [`SORTING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#sorting-dir) containing a [`SORTING`](outputs.qmd#sorting) saved to disk, and other metadata.

## Postprocessing

Postprocessing computes unit quality metrics used for curation.

**Inputs**

- a [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec) or [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC_LIST`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec-list),
  OR a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path) containing a [`PREPROCESSING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#preprocessing-dir) with saved recording.
- a [`CONFIG`](outputs.qmd#config)
- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path)

**Outputs**

- a [`POSTPROCESSING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#postprocessing-dir) containing a [`SORTING_ANALYZER`](outputs.qmd#sorting-analyzer) saved to disk as well as:
  - `POSTPROCESSING_PLOTS`](outputs.qmd#postprocessing-plots)
  - [`QUALITY_METRICS_CSV`](outputs.qmd#quality-metrics-csv) and other metadata.

<details>
<summary><strong>Postprocessing checks</strong></summary>

- must ensure the passed recording is the same recording used for sorting! (?)

</details>

## Curation

The curation step computes labels and merges automatically (e.g. with Bombcell, UnitRefine, SlaY) and applies them to the sorting analyzer, creating a new final sorting analyzer which services as the output of the pipeline.

**Inputs**

- a [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path) containing a [`POSTPROCESSING_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#postprocessing-dir) with a saved [`SORTING_ANALYZER`](outputs.qmd#sorting-analyzer)
- a [`CONFIG`](outputs.qmd#config)

**Outputs**

- a [`SORTING_ANALYZER`](outputs.qmd#sorting-analyzer) stored in the [`CURATION_DIR`](directory-definitions.qmd#curation-dir) and associated metadata.

<details>
<summary><strong>Curation checks</strong></summary>

- Confirm that the analyzer contains the extensions required by every enabled labeling or merge method.
- Confirm that all decision and merge unit IDs exist in the input analyzer, and that accepted merge groups do not conflict.
- Stop rather than overwrite the postprocessing analyzer or a pre-existing curation result unintentionally.
- Keep the preprocessed recording available when accepted merges require extension data to be recomputed from traces.
- Reload the saved final analyzer and verify that its unit IDs, labels, removals, and merges agree with [`CURATION_DECISIONS`](outputs.qmd#curation-decisions).

</details>
